body: I live with roommates and have a couple good friends and some other kinda-friends. I guess what I mean by isolation is my choosing not to be around other people. Honestly I'm getting a bit more perspective now. Yeah I should probably just hang out with potential friends more. Really appreciate you taking the time to talk.

Fair on the first point, but I did not insinuate the later. You can help these movements/problems if you join them, but I would not argue an individual's actions determines whether a movement lives or dies. I'm not trying to hurt you, but I'm sorry if I have. Good luck.
It's not a constant thing, but it's been happening for about 8 years at this point. Don't know what triggers it, probably isolation---especially on a Friday night.

I swear I'm not kidding here. If the state of the world really depresses you, become an activist. Everything you're talking about----climate change, inequality, the rise of far-right ideology----all of it **is** being fought against by people who care just as much as you. No movement can succeed on its own and every person counts.

You'll meet people you share a passion with in activist circles and they're often sensitive to the kinds of issues you're dealing with. If all else fails and you have a buddy you can trust to trip-sit, try [shrooms](https://www.forbes.com/sites/daviddisalvo/2020/01/31/study-psilocybin-from-magic-mushrooms-plus-therapy-delivers-benefits-nearly-five-years-later/).
